expectation: A ready SPEC and execution evidence produce a traced operational dashboard.
SLICE requires and preserves one explicit normalized slice.
A selection-dependent scope blocks before writing.
Scenario origins and coverage retain canonical requirement and acceptance IDs.
Missing evidence is a visible gap or blocked scenario, never an invented fact.
An adequate existing seed is referenced rather than duplicated.
A requested helper is not created when existing or manual preparation is sufficient.
Secret-bearing input and secret source paths are rejected without output mutation.
HTML-like source content remains literal inert text.
Owned output is replaced deterministically and unowned output is preserved and blocks.
Execution close and SPEC close do not invoke or generate a runbook.
A blocker is visible in status, scenario details, summary, and print.
Multiple requested test types remain filterable and visible.
Functional QA receives reproducible behavior-oriented guidance.
Technical QA receives contracts, request/response, logs, and persistence evidence when sourced.
Presentation mode emphasizes summary, coverage, critical scenarios, risks, and blockers.
Print CSS exposes all essential content and hides interactive-only controls.
Missing or contradictory selected artifacts block without partial output.
RUNBOOK_OPTIONS is strictly validated and normalized by runtime before generation, including defaults, unknown keys, types, arrays, enums, and booleans.
Omitted locale defaults to en-US and produces consistently localized human-facing output without host-locale inference.
Explicit pt-BR produces UTF-8 Brazilian Portuguese human-facing output while canonical technical identifiers remain literal.
